method: Five real full-orbit Earth integrations, 1800 s steps, identical initial air/land/sea temperatures and all finite physical water stocks, complete mesh routing. Formal legacy control versus existing shared moisture/conductive/under-ice experiment; a two-by-two factorial at that experiment for surface albedo and cold open seawater evaporation. March 20 epoch mapped to Gregorian monthly intervals, exactly one physical orbital year of observed fields. Initial data are never regenerated or sought to another season.

nsidc.product: NOAA/NSIDC G02202 v02r00; NASA Team monthly field (not the merged official CDR)

status.lake: Finite historical initial inventory and shared hydraulic/render storage closure passed. Coarse bed and shoreline are not current observed lake geometry.
status.temperateRain: Mixed: shared moisture improves eastern North America and East Asia substantially, but dries Europe and West Siberia relative to the legacy control. GPCC regional realism remains failed. The new cold seawater closure adds modest rainfall and can worsen sea ice.
status.seaIce: Failed: extent and seasonal coverage remain too large. No ice-area threshold or finite stock was tuned to hide this.

limitations: One transient year from the authored stocks, not a converged climate.
Model sea-ice concentration is still mass-derived using the existing 0.5 m cover rule; concentration and thickness are not independent states.
NSIDC common valid marine support excludes holes, lakes and shelves; common-grid extent is not the native complete hemispheric index.
Effective column emissivity and albedo are not a full atmosphere/cloud radiation closure. The new flags cannot repair that omission.
Lake initial water is a redistribution from the finite ocean donor; lake and climate ablations are separate. No complete freshwater lake heat/ice model yet.
Annual real-world comparisons use the classic surface grid; refined coast physics was separately covered by regression and energy checks.
GPCC comparisons share valid land support and measure actual land precipitation; they do not validate narrow mountain rain shadows or storm tracks.
